target_name: Knowledge Solvency Net Of Burn Per Claim
rationale: The construction is internally coherent and monotone in the intended direction (burn hurts through both numerator and denominator), but it is fundamentally a hybrid recombination of two already-evaluated archive signals rather than new economic content, so the marginal information is limited and largely diagnostic.

This is a pure mechanical industry-demeaning of an already-evaluated archive signal with no change in economic content — a useful robustness check but not a distinct signal proposal, and the archive already contains an IND_ZSCORE variant of the leverage family.

target_name: Knowledge Capitalized Five Year Earnings Record
rationale: TS_SUM(ib+xrd)/at is a near-linear combination of two long-published anomalies (cumulative profitability/earnings-to-assets and R&D-to-assets), and it is also a level-form restatement of the archive's "Expensing Induced Loss Illusion," so any positive result is uninterpretable as novel cross-theme evidence.

A one-year DELTA of a ratio whose numerator is a five-year sum reduces mostly to R&D-growth minus loss-change plus a large negative loading on asset growth, so the signal is confounded with two documented anomalies (R&D growth, asset growth) rather than isolating the claimed "revision in true solvency."

This is the only proposal that introduces genuinely new economic content (research output rather than input), but the positive expected sign sits uneasily with the well-documented negative sales-growth/investment premium and the mixed R&D-plus-liabilities denominator can become very small for cash-rich debt-free firms, so the interpretation will hinge on whether the scaling truly flips the sign.

target_name: Cash Tax Verified Return On Knowledge Capital
rationale: Internally inconsistent — txt is accrual-basis total tax expense, not cash taxes paid, so it does not deliver the "hard-to-fake" verification the hypothesis rests on, and cumulative tax expense over a capital base is in practice a rescaled profitability measure, i.e. a rediscovery of the profitability premium.
